explanation:
### How it works

When either target word appears, its closest preceding occurrence of the other target is the most recently seen one. Keep only those two indices.

### Steps

1. Initialize both target positions as unseen.
2. Update the appropriate position when a target appears.
3. Compare the current index to the latest opposite target.
4. Keep the smallest distance.

### Complexity

- Time: O(n) word comparisons.
- Space: O(1) auxiliary space.

alternatives.explanation:
### How it works

Collect the sorted positions of each target. Advancing the smaller position is sufficient because keeping it while moving the larger position can only increase their distance.

### Steps

1. Collect both target index lists.
2. Compare their current positions.
3. Advance the pointer at the smaller position.
4. Return the minimum difference encountered.

### Complexity

- Time: O(n) word comparisons.
- Space: O(n) for occurrence lists.
